text: Caroline "Tottie" Goldsmith OAM (born 27 August 1962) is an Australian actress and singer known for her roles as Trixie Sheldon in Starting Out, Toni Sheffield in The Young Doctors, Marilyn "Tex" Perez in Fire, and Cassandra Freedman in Neighbours. She hosted the Network Ten program Sex/Life in 1996 and was a contestant on the 8th season of the Australian version of I'm a Celebrity...Get Me Out of Here! in 2022. A founding member of the Chantoozies, a pop group formed in 1986, she was one of four female lead vocalists from 1986 until she left to pursue a solo singing career before the band released their second album, Gild the Lily in 1991. She rejoined the group temporarily in 2006 for the Countdown Spectacular concert series and permanently in 2012, before leaving again in 2020. With Chantoozies member Eve von Bibra, she performed as the duo the Toozies, who opened for the 2010 Antenna Awards. On 8 January 2023, she returned to music after a three-year break by performing with the 3XY Allstars in St. Kilda, and on 30 July 2023, invited former bandmate Ally Fowler to cover Olivia Newton-John's "You're the One That I Want," her first performance with a Chantoozies member since leaving the band. She also returned to the Chantoozies at a concert at the Sandstone Point Hotel on the Sunshine Coast on 26 July, filling in for Fowler. In the late 1990s, she co-hosted a breakfast program on Melbourne radio station TTFM, replacing Nicky Buckley. She played Janet in a season of the New Rocky Horror Show and participated in an arena version of Grease. Goldsmith works as a marriage celebrant and has released two meditation and relaxation albums: Unwind Your Mind (2004) and Falling Asleep (2005). After experiencing chronic fatigue syndrome and long-term sleep issues, she partnered with sleep specialist Chris Bunney to record Falling Asleep, which has since been prescribed by doctors. In 2007, she collaborated with a child psychologist on A Sleep Story, aimed at children. She was known as a sex symbol early in her career and posed nude for art magazine Black+White in August 1996. She is the daughter of Melbourne restaurateur and nightclub owner Brian Goldsmith and British-born actress Rona Newton-John (1941–2013), with her great-grandfather, the father of her grandmother Irene, being German-British physicist, mathematician, and Nobel Prize winner Max Born. Olivia Newton-John is her maternal aunt, Brett Goldsmith is her elder brother, and racecar driver Emerson Newton-John is her half brother; she has six other siblings. Goldsmith was married to skier Steven Lee, with whom she has one daughter, and became engaged to businessman James Mayo in January 2008. In the 2020 Queen's Birthday Honours, she was awarded the Medal of the Order of Australia (OAM) for "service to the community, and to the performing arts." She made guest appearances in Australian television series such as The Young Doctors, Starting Out, Prisoner, Saturdee, The Henderson Kids, Mission: Impossible (1989 episode), G.P., and Embassy. In 1996, she starred as Marilyn "Tex" Perez in the second season of Fire and also hosted Sex/Life, appeared in Twisted Tales and Shark Bay, and was a panellist on Beauty and the Beast and All-Star Squares. In the 2000s, she made guest appearances on The Secret Life of Us, Bert's Family Feud, Big Questions, Surprise Surprise Gotcha, Pizza, and Celebrity Singing Bee, and had a three-episode run on Blue Heelers. She appeared in a 2001 episode of Stingers and another in 2004. In 2009, she appeared in Neighbours for three months as Cassandra Freedman. She acted in two episodes of Swift and Shift Couriers, appeared in the 2010 film Ricky! The Movie as the ex-girlfriend of Ricky T, and as a gangster's girlfriend in the 2011 television film Underbelly Files: Infiltration. She had a supporting role in the 2012 Jack Irish telefilm Bad Debts. The Chantoozies released four singles: "Witch Queen", "He's Gonna Step On You Again", "Wanna Be Up", "Kiss and Tell", and an album, Chantoozies.
